paper_metadata.title: Superplasticity and High-Strength in Al-Zn-Mg-Zr Alloy with Ultrafine Grains

evidence.quote: the ultrafine -grained (UFG) 7xxx series alloy Al -4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr demonstrates superplasticity at unusually low temperatures of 120 -170°C while maintaining its high-strength state.
In this work aluminum alloy of the 7xxx series was used as the material for study with chemical composition as follows: Al -4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr (wt. %).
superplastic deformation of the UFG alloy Al -4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr is caused by the mechanism of grain-boundary sliding.
In this work, the ultrafine -grained (UFG) 7xxx series alloy Al -4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr demonstrates superplasticity at unusually low temperatures of 120 -170°C while maintaining its high-strength state.
HPT processing of the alloy Al-4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr at RT led to the formation of the UFG structure, as shown in Figure 1a. Quantitative analysis showed that the mean grain size was 17613 nm.
A number of initial samples were subjected to conventional treatment Т 6 that is recommended for achieving maximum hardening in the 7xxx s eries alloys [16].
In the UFG structure of the alloy, no noticeable change in the mean grain size after annealing for 1 hour at 120 °С was observed. The grain size is 19710 nm.
After annealing at 150, 170 and 200 С, the mean grain size of the alloy increased to 223 16, 29412 and 38511 nm, respectively.

The application of HPT processing contributes to the formation of homogeneous ultrafine-grained structure in the alloy Al -Zn-Mg-Zr under study with a mean grain size of ~170 nm that remains sufficiently stable up to the temperatures of 120 -150°C.

TEM studies of the UFG alloy structure ( Figure 6) after superplastic deformation at a temperature of 170°C and strain rate of 10 –3 s–1 showed certain increase in the mean grain size to 338±20 n m, but the grain shape remains equiaxial.

evidence.quote: It is well known that superplasticity is associated with grain boundary sliding (GBS )

the presence of nano -sized particles, clusters and grain -boundary segregations in the UFG structure makes it possible to achieve a unique level of strength by additional hardening mechanisms associated with these nanostructural features

The absence of noticeable changes in the grain shape and t he developed intragranular dislocation structure directly indicates that superplastic deformation of the UFG alloy Al -4.8Zn-1.2Mg-0.14Zr is caused by the mechanism of grain-boundary sliding.

There are high chances that HPT similarly causes the formation of Zn segregations at grain boundaries in the UFG alloy Al-Zn-Mg studied in the present work; such segregations activating GB sliding, which leads to a decrease in temperature of superplasticity effect.
